transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I keep blowing up at people over nothing. I’m snapping on operations calls, even at my family, and that’s just not how I’ve ever handled things before.
Did something stressful happen in your life shortly before you started getting this irritable?
Yeah. It started about three weeks ago, after the valve failure and the injury at the facility.
Since the valve failure and injury at the facility, have you been having recurring unwanted memories of it?

Yeah. I’ll be at the kitchen table or answering emails from home, and all of a sudden I’m back there—seeing the flash from the valve and the smoke in the aisle. It just pushes everything else out of my head.
Have you been having nightmares about the valve failure and injury?

Yeah. Most nights I’m lying there hearing that alarm in my head. When I finally fall asleep, I wake up sweating from dreams about smoke and people yelling. By morning, it feels like I barely slept at all.
Have you been avoiding reminders of the valve failure and injury?
I’m not sure what you mean by avoiding reminders. I haven’t really noticed myself doing that.
Since the valve failure, have you been feeling constantly on guard or easily startled?
Yeah. Any time I hear a forklift beep, a compressor kick on, even the smoke alarm chirp at home, my whole body just tightens up. I start looking for exits and thinking about what could go wrong next.
Since the valve failure, have you been going out of your way to avoid places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?
I don’t know. I haven’t really thought of it that way or noticed myself going out of my way to avoid things.
During the valve failure, did you think that you or someone else might die or be seriously injured?
I’m not sure. I don’t really know what I was thinking in that moment.
When these memories hit, does it ever feel like you’re actually back at the facility and reliving the valve failure in that moment?

Yeah. I can be at the kitchen table or answering emails at home, and all of a sudden I’m back there—seeing the flash from the valve and the smoke in the aisle. It kind of pushes everything else out of my head.
Have these symptoms been going on for a full month yet?
No, it hasn’t been a full month. It’s been about three weeks, since the valve failure and the injury at the facility.
Since the valve failure, have you been avoiding thoughts or feelings about what happened?
I’m not really sure what you mean by avoiding them. I mean, I try to get through the day, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m pushing the thoughts away.
Since the valve failure, have you been feeling persistently down, hopeless, or unable to feel positive emotions?

I don’t really feel glad about things like I normally would. My wife makes dinner, or the kids tell me about soccer, and I know I should be happy to be there with them, but… it’s like there’s nothing in me that responds.
Are there important parts of what happened during the valve failure that you still can’t remember?

Yeah. There are chunks I just can’t pull up—especially those seconds around the alarm and the shutdown. People keep telling me I did the right things, but I can’t really remember that part, and that scares me.
Since the valve failure, have there been times when you felt detached from yourself, like you were watching yourself from outside your body?
I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed feeling like I was outside my body or watching myself, no.
Since the valve failure, have you been avoiding the facility?
I’m not sure what you mean by avoiding it. I haven’t really noticed myself doing that.
Since the valve failure, have you been steering clear of anything that reminds you of it?
I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t really noticed myself deliberately staying away from reminders.
Since this started, have these symptoms been interfering with your ability to do your job or handle things at home?

Yeah. I haven’t been cleared to go back to the plant, and even from home I’m missing things on calls. I’ve upset people, and honestly I’m starting to worry I’m becoming a liability instead of the manager they need.
Since the valve failure, have you been trying not to think about what happened?
I don’t know that I’ve been trying to block it out or anything. It’s not something I’ve really noticed myself doing.
Since the valve failure, have you found yourself blaming yourself or someone else for what happened?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really caught myself blaming anybody, or blaming myself, exactly.
Since the valve failure, have you been avoiding thinking or talking about what happened?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself avoiding talking about it, exactly.
